title: Effective Generation of Feasible Solutions for Integer Programming via Guided Diffusion

problem.claim: Integer programming benefits substantially from feasible solutions that speed up solving, while similar instances may share structures and solution distributions that can be modeled.

gap.claim: Existing deep-learning approaches generate only partial feasible solutions and depend on solvers to complete them.

contributions.claim: An end-to-end framework generates complete feasible solutions for integer programming.

The framework uses contrastive learning to learn latent embeddings for integer-programming instances and their solutions, then uses diffusion models with guided sampling conditioned on instance representations and accounting for constraints and objectives.
The method's sampled partial solutions can be integrated with SCIP's CompleteSol heuristic to improve feasible-solution performance.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present their framework for generating complete feasible solutions end-to-end as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Across four typical integer-programming datasets, the framework generated complete feasible solutions with probability greater than 89.7% without relying on solvers, with solution quality comparable to Gurobi's best heuristic solutions.

When integrated with SCIP's CompleteSol heuristic, the method reportedly outperformed state-of-the-art methods across all datasets, improving the gap to optimal values by 3.7% to 33.7% and maintaining a feasible ratio above 99.7% on all datasets.

narrative_sequence.summary: Feasible solutions are important for accelerating integer-programming solving.
Similar integer-programming instances may exhibit shared structures and solution distributions suitable for deep-learning modeling.
Existing learning-based methods produce only partial feasible solutions and require solvers for completion.
The proposed framework learns instance and solution embeddings and uses conditioned diffusion with guided sampling to generate complete feasible solutions.
The authors report strong feasibility, solution-quality, and gap-to-optimality results across four datasets, including improved performance when combined with CompleteSol.

source_observation.claim: A solution-generation pipeline can combine representation learning with conditional diffusion and guidance based on constraints and objectives.

interpretation.claim: Separating instance-solution representation learning from constrained generative sampling may support direct generation of feasible candidates.

application.claim: For structured optimization tasks with repeated instance patterns, condition a generative model on instance representations and incorporate task constraints during sampling.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach generalizes beyond the four evaluated integer-programming datasets or to settings with substantially different structures.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify dataset identities, sizes, preprocessing, model architecture, training procedure, or evaluation protocol.
The abstract does not provide per-dataset results, baselines beyond named methods, or details of the guided sampling strategy.
